title: Signature in sound-mode of the exciton bilayer two-dimensional superfluid transition
authors: Giovanni Midei, Filippo Pascucci, Milorad V. Milosevìc, Jacques Tempere, David Neilson, Andrea Perali
abstract: Obtaining definitive evidence of exciton superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers in zero magnetic field remains a major longstanding challenge since the condensate is electrically neutral, making its phase coherence difficult to detect directly. We show that the Anderson-Bogoliubov sound velocity provides a dynamical signature of exciton superfluidity. Across the BCS-BEC crossover, the velocity is known to discontinuously drop to zero at the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition. The magnitude of the drop has a strong density dependence. We compute this behavior, with the inclusion of finite-temperature screening, and determine the BKT transition using a renormalization-group approach. We further identify a temperature window which is experimentally accessible, where vortex-antivortex excitations strongly renormalize both the sound velocity and the transition temperature.
summary: This work develops a theoretical method to detect exciton superfluidity in electron-hole bilayers by monitoring the Anderson-Bogoliubov sound velocity. The authors show that this velocity exhibits a sharp, measurable drop precisely at the BKT transition point. By incorporating finite-temperature screening and RG analysis, they provide an experimentally accessible signature for this neutral quantum phase.
main_problem: The primary challenge is obtaining definitive evidence of exciton superfluidity in electrically neutral electron-hole bilayers at zero magnetic field.
main_result: The Anderson-Bogoliubov sound velocity provides a measurable signature, showing a discontinuous drop to zero precisely at the Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) transition temperature.
method: Theoretical analysis using path integrals, Renormalization Group (RG) techniques for phase fluctuations, and solving gap equations incorporating finite-temperature screening.
model_or_system: The system is an exciton bilayer formed by parallel electron-hole layers. The model spans the BCS-BEC crossover regime, allowing tuning between weakly coupled and strongly coupled superfluid states.
key_observables: Anderson-Bogoliubov sound velocity ($c_s(T)$), phase stiffness ($J_0(T)$), compressibility ($\kappa_0(T)$), and the transition temperature ($T_{	ext{BKT}}^{	ext{RG}}$).
important_parameters: Carrier density, temperature (especially near $T_{	ext{BKT}}$), and the ratio of interaction types (contact vs. dipolar).
main_assumptions: The analysis often assumes low-density regimes where certain contributions (like spin-wave terms) can be neglected or approximated.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temperature dependence of various quantities, such as the maximum gap energy ($\Delta_{\max}$), polarization differences ($\Pi_N - \Pi_A$), and most critically, the sound velocity $c_s(T)$ tracking the superfluid transition.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the diagnostic observable (sound velocity) to developing the theoretical framework (RPA screening, RG flow) necessary to predict the BKT transition in this specific neutral exciton system.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, measurable dynamical signature ($c_s(T)$ collapse) for an elusive quantum phase (exciton superfluidity), bridging complex many-body theory with potential experimental detection methods.
